claims: RealTCD uses language-derived initial adjacency followed by numerical score optimization over temporal graphs and intervention targets.

The setup assumes causal sufficiency, a known observational regime, finite lag and a DAG on the unrolled variables; Theorem 3.1 is conditional on capacity, intervention faithfulness, positivity and entropy assumptions.
The real cooling-system study lacks a ground-truth DAG and scores selected relationships using expert physical-location rules.
adverse_findings_and_limits: The theorem is an author-stated population optimization result; local stochastic optimization and an edge threshold are not a finite-sample confidence guarantee.
Anomaly windows are modeled as intervention regimes. An anomaly is not by itself a verified exogenous intervention in a bank.
Useful temporal initialization candidate; not evidence for hidden-confounder identification or arbitrary bank state dynamics.

claims: NLPSCM combines sequential batches of observational data with a language model treated as a noisy expert and uses PAG representations.
The algorithm allocates a fixed language-model query budget to edges; empirical answer histograms and thresholds supply background information.
The paper reports graph metrics across models and a selected parameter-recovery example under misspecified priors.
sources.inspection_scope: Explicit selected passages, not an assertion that every page was reviewed.

anchors.section: Sequential-batch scope and contributions
Edge histograms, threshold and budgeted interaction
Cross-model results and parameter-recovery example

adverse_findings_and_limits: Sequential batching here concerns contemporaneous variables across data batches, not temporal causal identification or dynamic-treatment evaluation.
Approximate edge-answer histograms and semantic entropy do not establish simultaneous graph confidence or effect-set coverage.
Information-seeking model queries are not physical interventions; error guarantees require separate assumptions and proofs.
sources.project_disposition: Candidate PAG and budgeted-query baseline; require a formal bridge from uncertain graph outputs to effect sets before qualification.

claims: LCM is a supervised time-series foundation model that maps temporal samples to lagged adjacency tensors using convolution and transformer components.
The stated model assumes additive noise, causal stationarity, no latent confounders and no contemporaneous effects.
The limitations section says the model does not detect or correct violations of these assumptions.
sources.inspection_scope: Explicit selected passages, not an assertion that every page was reviewed.

anchors.section: Temporal SCM assumptions
Transformer architecture and training-distribution prior
Future work and explicit limitations

adverse_findings_and_limits: This is adjacent numerical foundation-model evidence, not a language-model-assisted discovery method.
Single-pass prediction and reported benchmark generalization do not establish uniform calibration or validity under hidden confounding/regime changes.
sources.project_disposition: Classify as an adjacent data-only comparator; do not advertise latent-temporal support from the title.

claims: The paper describes causal-learn+ with agent assistance for data inspection, assumption elicitation, method selection and interpretation around formal discovery algorithms.
It distinguishes agent suggestions, user decisions, algorithm parameters and graph outputs, and explains why CPDAG/PAG ambiguity must remain visible.
It calls for future benchmarks of data diagnosis, method selection and calibrated interpretation.
adverse_findings_and_limits: This is a design argument and system description, not an independently qualified bank workflow or measured institutional benefit.
User approval does not prove assumption truth, and formal algorithms remain conditional on their sampling and scientific premises.
A declared, separately validated hybrid method is conceptually possible; the paper’s restrictive design preference is not a universal impossibility theorem.

claims: MDA uses an LLM for executable mechanism proposals; numerical methods fit models, approximate evidence and select experimental designs.
The operational design criterion is a model-disagreement approximation to expected information gain, with BIC or SMC evidence and latent-state inference.
Reported studies cover chemistry, glucose ODEs and stochastic neuron dynamics; the paper explicitly states its finite held-out prediction tests do not establish causal identification.
The illustrated experiments use open-loop policies. Chemistry comparisons retain 115 matched evaluable world-seed cells from 171 attempts; inference comparisons share a model archive and histories.
adverse_findings_and_limits: An adaptively proposed and pruned model pool need not contain the truth. Normalized BIC weights and conditional posterior uncertainty are not uniform causal coverage.
The reported comparisons target sample efficiency and are not compute matched; failed/unavailable cells must remain in the denominator of a bank trial.
Mechanism proposals are an architectural candidate, not evidence of a qualified closed-loop servicing policy or of local reproduction.
